items.title: Show HN: HackerBooks – HackerTube, but for books mentioned on HN
items.raw_content: Saw Karpathy's HackerTube and wanted the same thing for books. So I had Claude build one (Opus 5.5). It's ~16.5k books that at least two different HN commenters brought up, from 2007 till now. Each book links back to the comments that mentioned it. Data is downloadable from the about page. To be clear: Claude wrote almost all of it, including the data pipeline and the site. I mostly steered and made calls, bought the domain name, etc. It counts mentions, so it's not perfect (praising a book and trashing it both count). If your favourite book is missing or matched to the wrong thing, tell me. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50326821 Points: 938 # Comments: 183

items.title: Show HN: OmniDiff – Opensource, super fast, content aware Git difftool, in Rust
items.raw_content: I have been researching what the ultimate diff tool would look like, based on actual diffs in open source repositories. OmniDiff can diff: code (25 languages), config, images, PDFs, archives, cursors, fonts... It's fast. It can diff C++ files of tens of thousands of lines in under 100ms, on a 2023 ThinkPad T14s. It's open source. AGPLv3. It's based on real diffs. I looked at the 7400 repositories that are listed in Gentoo packages, sampled 2000 diffs and solved them manually to get a good understanding of what is needed, before putting together the diff pipelines for each content type. Incidentally, this also forms the basis of the CI pipeline, so the robustness of the codebase is quite high. I'm still developing it. It's v0.3.0 at this time. But I have been using it daily as my git difftool for months now, and it works well. AI Disclosure: Yes, I do use AI. No, I do not vibecode. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50325253 Points: 164 # Comments: 41
items.title_zh: Show HN：OmniDiff——开源、高速、内容感知的 Rust Git 差异工具
items.summary: An open-source AGPLv3 Git difftool written in Rust, OmniDiff handles code in 25 languages plus configs, images, PDFs, archives, and fonts. Its author says it can diff tens of thousands of lines of C++ in under 100ms on a 2023 ThinkPad T14s.
